name: Work Permit for Foreign Residents (Management/Technical Roles)

requirements.blocker_text: Resolution 56/2026 of the Ministry of Labor and Social Security (signed 31 August 2026, published in Official Gazette No. 73 on 3 September 2026): foreign nationals holding temporary-resident, real-estate-resident, or humanitarian-resident classification who occupy management or specialized technical positions must obtain a Work Permit, 'except for expressly authorized exceptions.' This is separate from the parallel reform (Decree-Law 128, amending the 2014 Foreign Investment Law) that lets joint ventures hire CUBAN workers directly without mandatory state intermediation -- that specific change does not itself alter foreign nationals' own work-authorization requirement.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the specific residence classification held and apply for the Work Permit required for management/technical roles, unless an express exception applies.

evidence_required.document: Proof of qualifying residence classification (temporary, real-estate, or humanitarian resident)

outcome.duration_length: not specified in the sources reviewed

sources.title: CiberCuba (independent Cuba-focused press) -- Resolution 56/2026, Work Permit requirement for foreign nationals in management/technical roles

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Cuba). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to independent press reporting on a resolution published just 3 days before this build's verified_at date, tier 4; the Official Gazette No. 73 text itself could not be fetched (gacetaoficial.gob.cu timed out). EXTREMELY CURRENT FINDING: this resolution is part of a broader package Cuba calls its '176 Economic and Social Transformations,' approved in 2026, and was signed barely a week before this dataset's build date -- among the most recent legal changes documented anywhere in this dataset. The permit requirement is explicitly tied to which RESIDENCE classification a foreigner holds (temporary/real-estate/humanitarian) under the also-brand-new Ley de Extranjeria -- but that law was published 5 May 2026 and does not take legal effect until roughly 180 days later (~early November 2026), so the practical interplay between this September 2026 Work Permit resolution and the not-yet-effective residence-classification system is itself unresolved and worth a dedicated follow-up. citizenship_after_months (60) mirrors the standard naturalization threshold (see cu_citizenship_naturalisation.json). family_can_work left null: not addressed by the source.
